# sendgrid_subuser (Resource)

Manages a SendGrid subuser: an isolated sub-account with its own sending reputation, templates, and API keys, typically used to separate sending on behalf of different products or customers under one parent account.

~> SendGrid's API does not support changing a subuser's `username`, `email`, `password`, or `region` after creation; changing any of these forces recreation. `ips` and `disabled` can be updated in place.

~> SendGrid has no endpoint that returns a subuser's currently assigned IPs, so `ips` cannot be refreshed by `terraform plan` and is not populated by `terraform import`; on import, the first plan will show a change to `ips` and apply it via the update-IPs endpoint.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sendgrid_subuser" "app" {
  username = "my_app_subuser"
  email    = "subuser@example.com"
  password = var.subuser_password
  ips      = ["203.0.113.10"]
}

variable "subuser_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) The subuser's email address. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `ips` (List of String) The IP addresses assigned to this subuser. At least one is required at creation time; can be updated in place afterward.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password the subuser will use to log into SendGrid. Cannot be changed via this resource after creation.
- `username` (String) The subuser's username. Cannot be changed after creation.

### Optional

- `disabled` (Boolean) Whether this subuser is disabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `region` (String) The region this subuser is assigned to: `global` or `eu`. Defaults to `global`. Cannot be changed after creation.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The subuser's numeric user ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sendgrid_subuser.app <username>
```
